w: Its name is just a clipped mash-up of 'kunsti muuseum' - art museum - but Kumu is the flagship of the Art Museum of Estonia. The permanent collection tracks Estonian art from the 18th century through Soviet occupation, hanging Socialist Realism beside the nonconformist work made to defy it.
_facts: Name is a portmanteau of 'kunsti muuseum' (museum of art); one of the largest art museums in Northern Europe
Main branch of the Art Museum of Estonia, housing its offices
Permanent collection covers Estonian art from the 18th century, including Soviet-era Socialist Realism and Nonconformist art
Won the European Museum of the Year Award in 2008

w: Raised to beef up telecoms for the sailing events of the 1980 Moscow Olympics, this 313-metre concrete needle survived a fire mid-construction and still stands as the tallest structure in Tallinn. Its 21st-floor deck was designed with a rotating section and once closed for five years of renovation.
s: 313m of Soviet concrete, built for the Olympics
_facts: Built to support telecommunications for the sailing regatta of the 1980 Moscow Summer Olympics
313 m tall, the tallest nonbuilding structure in Tallinn; opened 11 July 1980
Observation deck (170m) closed 2007-2012 for renovation; survived a fire during construction
21st-floor deck originally designed to have a rotating section; stained glass by Dolores Hoffmann

w: Opened in 1980 as the V. I. Lenin Palace of Culture and Sports, this concrete brutalist hulk on the harbour once held concerts and an ice rink just beyond the Old Town walls - and even came with its own small seaport and a heliport. It now sits semi-abandoned, a monument to Soviet ambition gone quiet.
s: A brutalist palace of culture, now half-empty
_facts: Originally the V. I. Lenin Palace of Culture and Sports, completed 1980
Multipurpose venue with a concert hall and ice rink, located in the harbour just beyond the Old Town walls
Includes a heliport and small seaport; now semi-abandoned

w: The Estonian Song Festival, Laulupidu, fills these grounds with tens of thousands of singers every five years - a national choir turning open ground into the loudest place in Estonia for one weekend, then falling quiet again until the next one.
s: Where all of Estonia sings, every five years
_facts: Grounds on which the Estonian Song Festival 'Laulupidu' is held every five years

w: Nuns and monks lived side by side within these Bridgettine walls from 1407 until the convent was abandoned in 1575 - a double house that was, at 1,360 square metres, the largest church building anywhere in medieval Estonia and the biggest convent in all of Livonia. Its ruins still stand in Pirita today.
s: Medieval Estonia's biggest church, now ruins
_facts: Bridgettine convent for both nuns and monks, functioned 1407-1575
Largest convent in Livonia; at 1,360 sq m, the largest church building in medieval Estonia

w: Metsakalmistu means simply 'forest cemetery' - a wooded burial ground in the Pirita district where graves sit scattered among the pines rather than lined up in rows, a quiet contrast to the city's more formal graveyards.
s: A forest cemetery, graves among the pines
_facts: Metsakalmistu ('Forest Cemetery') is a cemetery in the Pirita district of Tallinn
